en: Many mistakenly think the common maya is the national bird, but the official national bird is actually the Philippine eagle.
Emilio Aguinaldo was the first president of the Philippines, not Jose Rizal, who never held any elected executive office.
Ferdinand Magellan did not discover the Philippines, as indigenous peoples already inhabited the archipelago thousands of years before his arrival.
While Emilio Aguinaldo designed the flag, Marcela Agoncillo and her daughters actually sewed the first official Philippine flag in Hong Kong.
Contrary to confusing names, the Senate and House of Representatives form the Legislative branch, which makes laws, rather than the Judicial branch.
Many believe Tagalog is the sole national language, but Filipino is the official national language incorporating words from various regional languages.
Supreme Court justices are not elected by voters, but are instead appointed by the President from a shortlist provided by the Judicial and Bar Council.
Lapu-Lapu was not a Tagalog ruler, but rather a Visayan chieftain of Mactan island in Cebu who defeated Ferdinand Magellan.
Although the US recognized Philippine independence on July 4, the country officially celebrates Independence Day on June 12 to honor the 1898 proclamation.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were not built with modern machinery, but carved entirely by hand by the indigenous Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago.
Ambrosio Rianzares Bautista, not Andres Bonifacio, was the actual author who read and wrote the original 1898 Philippine Declaration of Independence.
The Philippine national motto is not in English, but officially stated in Filipino as 'Maka-Diyos, Maka-tao, Makakalikasan at Makabansa'.
